## About Me

### A Brief Bio

The Christian liberal arts have been a driving force throughout my life. My early education at [Veritas School](https://veritasschool.net/) in Newberg, Oregon developed in my a passion for lifelong learning, which led me to study Mathematics and Computer Science at [Westmont College](https://www.westmont.edu/). I graduated in 2019, and—inspired by a summer of research with [Dr. Russell Howell](https://www.westmont.edu/people/russell-w-howell-phd)—pursued a Ph.D. in Mathematics at [UC Santa Barbara](https://www.math.ucsb.edu/). Under the direction of my advisor, [Dr. Fedya Manin](https://www.math.toronto.edu/manin/), I studied how nilpotent algebraic structures influence both the geometric behavior of topological spaces, as well as the patterns of aperiodic tilings. I defended [my thesis](media/papers/hansen-dissertation-2025-05-02.pdf) in 2025. That same fall, I returned with enthusiasm to Westmont College as an Assistant Professor of Mathematics. In my leisure time, I can be found [singing](https://quireofvoyces.org/), [reading](https://www.goodreads.com/kylehansen), [swimming](media/images/tri_swim.jpeg), [biking](media/images/tri_bike.jpeg), [running](media/images/tri_run.jpeg), (or [all three](https://www.santabarbaratriathlon.com/)), [baking](media/images/croissants.jpeg), and enjoying the company of [my church family](https://cpcsb.org/).

### Research Interests

#### Quantitative Topology
If you want to study the complexity of a topological space, you might study the algebraic invariants of this space.
Often, however, topological spaces such as manifolds come equipped with some geometric structure as well. 
How does this algebraic topological complexity translate into geometric complexity?
This broad question motivates the field of so-called "quantitative topology".

For example, if you have a nullhomotopic map (a priori, algebraic information) into your space, what is the most efficient way to perform this nullhomotopy (geometric information)?
My advisor [Fedya Manin](https://www.math.toronto.edu/manin/) has asked (and answered) similar questions in the context of simpy connected target spaces, and some of my current work is an extension of this to nilpotent targets.

I have also studied elliptic manifolds, where I asked "Given a nilpotent Lie group $G$, what algebraic information is necessary/sufficient to guarantee that a closed manifold $M$ is $G$-elliptic?" 
In some sense, this asks which manifolds $M$ can be efficiently wrapped using the group $G$ as your wrapping paper.
Recent advances in related areas have opened up some clear paths forward in this investigation, where it seems likely that the Heisenberg group is a poor choice of wrapping paper for a flat torus.

#### Tiling Spaces
I also study tiling spaces, where I am interested in extending some existing theory to the relevant nilpotent setting. 
For example, I extend work about the topology of Euclidean tiling spaces to tiling spaces of certain nilpotent Lie groups.
